brief.era: Late Victorian era, 1888, during the reign of Queen Victoria; London and Bohemia are depicted with period-accurate technology: gas lighting, hansom cabs, landaus, bicycles not yet common, telegrams and letters as primary long-distance communication.
brief.place: Primary action in London: Baker Street (Holmes' residence), Serpentine Avenue and Briony Lodge in St. John's Wood, Edgeware Road and Regent Street for the cab chase, Charing Cross station for Irene Adler's departure to the Continent. Secondary reference to Bohemia (Kingdom of Bohemia, Carlsbad, Egria) as the King's homeland and origin of the note paper.
brief.dress: Holmes: dressing gown, suit, various disguises (groom, clergyman). Watson: morning coat, military ulster. Irene Adler: elegant evening dress, bonnet, walking clothes, cloak. King of Bohemia/Count Von Kramm: rich Bohemian noble attire (astrakhan-trimmed coat, deep blue cloak with flame-coloured silk lining, flaming beryl brooch, fur-trimmed boots, broad-brimmed hat, black vizard mask). Godfrey Norton: lawyer's attire, likely dark suit. Clergyman: surplice, clerical garments. Servants and street workers: period-appropriate uniforms (ostlers, scissors-grinder, coachman, loafers in shabby dress, guardsmen in uniform).
brief.buildings_and_objects: 221B Baker Street: Victorian terraced house with sitting room, bedroom, drawing-room, table with cigars and spirit case, gasogene, fireplace, bell-pull. Briony Lodge: bijou two-story villa with garden, sitting room with long windows and preposterous English window fasteners, drawing-room, hall, principal room with couch, recess behind sliding panel above right bell-pull. Church of St. Monica: modest urban church with altar, side aisle, surpliced clergyman. Hansom cab, landau, brougham: horse-drawn carriages. Plumber's smoke-rocket: cigar-shaped, self-lighting device used in fire alarm ruse. Telegram, note paper, photograph (cabinet size), letter, emerald snake ring, gold watch, sovereign coin, tobacco pouch, shag tobacco, half-and-half drink.
depiction_rules: Sherlock Holmes should be depicted as sharp-featured, observant, with intense gaze; never as a romantic or emotional figure, but as a man of reason. His disguises are convincing but retain his underlying physiognomy. Irene Adler must be shown as a woman of striking beauty and resolute expression, never as a passive victim; her intelligence and agency are central. The King of Bohemia should be depicted as a man of regal bearing, even in disguise, with visible distress and grandeur. Watson is a loyal, middle-aged doctor, not a fool, but often amazed by Holmes's deductions. Avoid melodrama; emphasize quiet observation, subtle gestures, and the tension of wits. The fire alarm ruse must show the smoke-rocket thrown through an open window, not an actual fire. No supernatural elements; all solutions are logical and observation-based.
